description: How electric motors convert energy and how robots drive them: DC, brushless and stepper motors, H-bridges, closed-loop control, servos, batteries and gearing. Students model motors, simulate drives on the circuit bench, and build and tune a small motor controller on the hardware bench.
modelledOn: Mohan, Undeland and Robbins, Power Electronics: Converters, Applications and Design
Franklin, Powell and Emami-Naeini, Feedback Control of Dynamic Systems
outcomes: Derive the equivalent-circuit and torque-speed model of a DC motor and identify its parameters from measurements.
Select between brushed, brushless and stepper motors for a given torque, speed and cost requirement.
Design an H-bridge PWM drive with correct dead time, flyback protection and current limiting.
Tune cascaded current, speed and position loops and judge them by step response.
Compute a battery and power budget for a mobile robot and choose a gear ratio that matches motor and load.

units.title: Energy conversion and electromechanics
topics: Magnetic circuits: flux, reluctance, Faraday's law and the Lorentz force
Torque production and back-EMF as the two faces of one coupling
Power flow and losses: copper, iron and friction; efficiency maps
Mechanical load models: constant torque, viscous, fan and inertial loads; the torque-speed plane
Sizing a motor for a duty cycle: peak, continuous and RMS torque

units.title: DC motor models
topics: The permanent-magnet DC motor equivalent circuit: armature resistance, inductance, torque and back-EMF constants
Torque-speed and current-speed lines; stall torque and no-load speed
Electromechanical transfer function: electrical and mechanical time constants
Separately excited, shunt, series and compound DC machines
Speed control by armature voltage and by field weakening
Parameter identification from no-load and locked-rotor tests

units.title: Brushless, stepper and AC motors
topics: Stepper motors: variable reluctance, permanent magnet and hybrid; full, half and microstepping
Stepper torque-speed behaviour: resonance, missed steps and current chopping
Brushless DC motors: construction, Hall-sensor commutation and the six-step sequence
Sensorless commutation by back-EMF and an introduction to field-oriented control
Induction and synchronous motors: rotating field, slip and the V/f relation
Choosing a motor type for a robot joint, wheel, pump or conveyor

units.title: H-bridges and power electronics
topics: Power MOSFETs and IGBTs as switches: gate drive, conduction and switching losses
The H-bridge: four-quadrant operation, braking and shoot-through with dead time
PWM generation: duty cycle, frequency choice and average voltage
Inductive loads: flyback diodes, current ripple and voltage spikes
Motor driver ICs, current sensing, overcurrent and thermal protection

units.title: Motor drive control
topics: Open-loop drives: voltage-frequency control and stepper pulse trains
Closed-loop speed control with a PI controller
Cascaded current and speed loops; loop bandwidths
Feedback sensing: optical encoders, quadrature decoding, tachometers and Hall sensors
PID tuning: Ziegler-Nichols, step-response methods and anti-windup
Current limiting, dynamic braking and regenerative braking

units.title: Servo systems
topics: Servo architecture: hobby servo PWM protocol versus an industrial servo drive
Position control loop: step response, overshoot, settling time and steady-state error
Motion profiles: trapezoidal and S-curve acceleration limits
Multi-axis coordination for a robot arm and a differential-drive base
Friction, backlash and disturbance compensation; feedforward

units.title: Batteries and power budgets
topics: Battery chemistries: lead-acid, Li-ion and LiFePO4; capacity, C-rate and energy density
Discharge curves, internal resistance, state of charge and Peukert's effect
Battery management: cell balancing, protection and charge profiles
Power budget of a mobile robot: duty cycles, peak currents and runtime estimates
Solar charging and off-grid operation for a field robot in Ghana
Regulated rails: DC-DC conversion for logic, sensors and motors

units.title: Gearing and transmission
topics: Gear ratio, torque-speed trade and reflected inertia
Efficiency, backlash and wear in spur, helical and worm gears
Planetary and harmonic drives; gear trains
Belts, chains, lead screws and linear actuators
Matching motor and load: the optimum gear ratio and thermal limits

schedule.title: Magnetics, torque and back-EMF
schedule.exercise: Compute the force on a 0.1 m conductor carrying 5 A in a 0.8 T field, show that torque constant and back-EMF constant are numerically equal in SI units, and list the loss terms in a motor.

tasks.title: Plot the back-EMF of a motor against speed from 0 to 3000 rpm for a given constant and read the voltage at 1500 rpm
Given measured input power and shaft power at six loads, compute and plot efficiency and find the load where efficiency peaks
Compute reluctance and flux for a gapped iron core at three gap lengths and show how the air gap dominates the magnetic circuit

schedule.title: Loads and motor sizing
schedule.exercise: Size a motor for a market-stall conveyor that lifts 20 kg at 0.2 m/s with a 40 percent duty cycle, giving peak and RMS torque and the continuous rating needed.

tasks.title: Plot the torque-speed curves of a constant-torque load and a fan load on one graph and mark where each meets a motor line
Compute RMS torque for a four-phase duty cycle of accelerate, run, decelerate and rest, and check it against a motor continuous rating
Choose between three catalogue motors for a given load profile by checking peak torque, RMS torque, speed and cost, and justify the pick

schedule.title: The permanent-magnet DC motor
schedule.exercise: Derive the transfer function from armature voltage to speed, compute the electrical and mechanical time constants from given parameters, and sketch the step response.

tasks.title: Plot the torque-speed and current-speed lines of a given DC motor and read off stall torque, stall current and no-load speed
Model a DC motor as a resistor, inductor and back-EMF source in the bench, apply 12 V, and record the start-up current spike
Simulate the speed step response for three rotor inertias and compare each mechanical time constant with the value derived by hand

schedule.title: DC machine types, speed control and identification
schedule.exercise: From a no-load test and a locked-rotor test on a small motor, compute armature resistance, torque constant and viscous friction, and predict its speed at 8 V under a given load.

tasks.title: Vary the armature voltage of a simulated motor from 2 to 12 V in steps and plot steady speed against voltage
Measure the no-load current and speed of a small DC motor at two supply voltages with a sensor and derive its torque constant
Compare the torque-speed curves of shunt and series motors in a plot and explain why a series motor suits starting heavy loads

schedule.title: Stepper motors
schedule.exercise: For a 200-step motor with a 1.8 degree step, compute step rate for 300 rpm in full and 1/16 microstepping, and explain why torque falls as step rate rises.

tasks.title: Drive a stepper motor with a full-step sequence from an Arduino and count steps to turn the shaft exactly one revolution
Compare full, half and 1/8 microstepping on the same motor by recording smoothness and the maximum step rate before stalling
Ramp the step rate of a loaded stepper until it misses steps, plot the pull-out curve, and add acceleration to extend it

schedule.title: Brushless and AC motors, and choosing a motor type
schedule.exercise: Write the six-step commutation table for a three-phase BLDC motor given the Hall sensor codes, and rank brushed, brushless and stepper motors for a drone, a wheelchair and a 3D printer.

tasks.title: Fill the six-step commutation table from Hall sensor states and plot the three phase currents over one electrical cycle
Simulate a three-phase inverter driving a BLDC motor in six-step mode and measure back-EMF zero crossings for sensorless timing
Select and justify a motor type for three robot scenarios in a case study, scored on torque, noise, cost, efficiency and drive complexity

schedule.title: H-bridges and motor drivers
schedule.exercise: Draw the current paths in an H-bridge for forward drive, coast and brake, calculate the dead time needed for given switching times, and size the MOSFET for a 5 A motor.

tasks.title: Drive a DC motor model with PWM at 20, 50 and 80 percent duty and record the average voltage and resulting speed
Build an H-bridge from four MOSFETs and reverse the motor, then provoke shoot-through and measure the current spike
Remove the flyback diodes from an H-bridge driving an inductive load, record the voltage spike, and restore a safe design with clamping

schedule.title: Speed control loops
schedule.exercise: Design a PI speed controller for a motor with a 50 ms mechanical time constant to reach a setpoint within 0.2 s without overshoot, and explain why the current loop must be faster.

tasks.title: Apply a proportional gain to a simulated motor speed loop and read the steady-state error for gains of 1, 5 and 20
Code a PI speed controller for a first-order motor model and tune it for under 5 percent overshoot and 0.3 s settling
Build an inner current loop and an outer speed loop in code and show the response when the load torque steps up mid-run

schedule.title: Feedback sensors, tuning and braking
schedule.exercise: Compute the speed resolution of a 500-count encoder read at 100 Hz, tune a PID with the Ziegler-Nichols step method, and compare dynamic and regenerative braking energy flows.

tasks.title: Read a quadrature encoder on an Arduino, turn the shaft by hand, and confirm direction and count for one full revolution
Tune a PID speed loop using the Ziegler-Nichols method on a simulated motor and compare its step response with a hand-tuned PI
Add anti-windup to a saturating speed controller, then show with and without it how a long stall affects recovery of the setpoint

schedule.title: Servo systems and motion profiles
schedule.exercise: Generate a trapezoidal motion profile for a 90 degree move with limits on speed and acceleration, and predict the tracking error caused by friction without feedforward.

tasks.title: Drive a hobby servo with 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 ms pulses from an Arduino and record the angle reached for each
Code a trapezoidal motion profile with speed and acceleration limits and plot position, velocity and acceleration for a 90 degree move
Simulate a position servo with Coulomb friction and backlash, measure the limit cycle, and reduce it with feedforward and a dead-band

schedule.title: Battery behaviour and management
schedule.exercise: From a datasheet discharge curve, estimate capacity at 0.2C and 1C for a 2000 mAh Li-ion cell, and list the protections a battery pack needs before it is mounted on a robot.

tasks.title: Convert battery ratings from mAh and voltage to watt-hours for four chemistries and rank them by energy per kilogram
Plot voltage against state of charge for a cell at two C-rates and read the usable capacity before the cut-off voltage
Model a battery as a source with internal resistance, simulate a motor start-up current spike, and show how the voltage dip resets the controller

schedule.title: Power budgets, solar charging and regulated rails
schedule.exercise: Build a power budget table for a field robot with two drive motors, a sensor mast and a radio, then size the solar panel and battery for six hours of operation in Tamale sunlight.

tasks.title: Fill a power budget for a robot with five loads, compute average current and estimate runtime from a 5 Ah battery
Power a microcontroller and a servo from one battery through two regulated rails and measure the rail dip when the servo moves
Size a solar panel and battery for a field robot using hourly sunshine data for northern Ghana and test that the budget balances over a week

schedule.title: Gearing and matching motor to load
schedule.exercise: For a wheel driven through a gearbox, compute the gear ratio that maximises acceleration given motor inertia and wheel inertia, and check the motor stays below its thermal limit.

tasks.title: Compute output torque and speed through gear ratios 1:5, 1:20 and 1:100 for a given motor, including a 90 percent efficiency per stage
Convert motor rotation to linear travel for a lead screw and a belt drive, and compare speed, force and resolution for each
Find the optimum gear ratio for a given load inertia, plot acceleration against ratio, and verify the chosen motor stays within thermal limits
